title: Hosted EdgeBundle PRD — Minimal Generation + Embeddings + Rerank Surface and Progressive Cutover Guide
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: This PRD defines a minimal, consistent API surface (EdgeBundle) that bundles chat/completions (generation), embeddings, and rerank in a compact hosted offering for early enterprise customers. The goal is to deliver a small set of deterministic, observable behaviors with progressive rollout and fallbacks so product teams can adopt hosted endpoints without re-architecting. This doc clarifies requirements, enumerates scope changes compared to broader Hosted API initiatives, and provides a prescriptive launch and cutover guide.

Goals: Provide a single lightweight surface for common workflows (1) conversational generation (chat/completions), (2) embedding vectors, and (3) candidate reranking. Prioritize predictable latency, clear cost controls, and compatibility with Redwood routing/fallbacks.

Non-goals: This PRD does not include multimodal inputs (images/audio), native streaming-only experimental transports, or custom model hosting for dedicated/private customers. Those are handled under other initiatives.

Key clarifications/decisions since kickoff: 1) Minimal parameter set: support prompt/messages, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop, and model selector. 2) Deterministic embedding config: fixed dimensionality per model family with clear normalization contract. 3) Rerank API accepts up to 100 candidates in ranked mode; long-list scoring will be deferred. 4) Fallback policy: if preferred model is unavailable, route to a compatible lower-cost variant with delta-notification in response headers.
api_surface: POST /v1/edgebundle/generate — accepts messages OR prompt; returns tokens + token_metadata + deterministic ids
POST /v1/edgebundle/embeddings — accepts batch inputs up to 256 items; returns vectors (float32/quantized), model id, and vector_norm metadata
POST /v1/edgebundle/rerank — accepts (query, candidates[]) and returns ranked indices and per-candidate scores; supports explain=false/true
Headers: X-Model-Variant, X-Fallback-Info, X-Request-Trace for tracing and billing attribution
Streaming: optional SSE for generate with chunked tokens; if SSE not negotiated, return complete response when generation completes
behavioral_contracts: Determinism: same model+seed+inputs => identical top-1 output for deterministic mode (temperature=0).
Cost-protection: API returns token_estimate header based on model profile; large batches rejected with 413 and helpful guidance.
Latency SLAs: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for small prompts (<=64 tokens) on dedicated lanes; hosted best-effort but must provide per-request latency metadata.
Quality regression: automated eval harness comparing Canary model outputs against baseline evaluation suite; regressions blocked before rollout.
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal): Enable internal teams and Solutions Eng to test endpoints — 1 week
Closed Beta: 5 customers (mix of AI-native and enterprise) with traffic caps and a dedicated support contact — 2 weeks
Graduated Canary: 10% traffic slice across regions with automatic rollback on metrics (error_rate>1% or quality_drop>2%) — 1 week
General availability: step up traffic in 25% increments after 72h stability windows, full GA when billing SDK and SLAs enabled
acceptance_criteria: API contract: All endpoints conform to the documented schema and return 2xx/4xx/5xx semantics consistently
E2E tests: Passes generation/embedding/rerank E2E suites in staging and preflight (deterministic checks for seeded cases)
Benchmarks: Token throughput and p95 latency within 15% of target profiles for the release on host lanes
Telemetry: Per-request token counts, latency, cost attribution and fallback flags are emitted and wired to dashboards
Safety: Must integrate content-safety filter (service-level guards) and return action_code when content blocked
Docs/SDK: Public docs, quickstart, and SDK examples for Node/Python deployed alongside GA
Rollback tested: Automated rollback triggers validated in dry-run (simulate threshold breach and verify rollbacks occur and traffic rebalances)
launch_checklist: Finalize API RFC and publish to team — include sample payloads for edge-cases
Engineering: complete feature branches and merge to release candidate; attach PR links
Performance: run regional perf suites (us-west1, eu-west1) and publish runbook with observed profiles
Telemetry: create dashboards (edgebundle-overview, errors-by-model, fallback-rate) and define alert thresholds
Security/Compliance: complete KMS integration QA and sign-off from security reviewer
Support/Docs: publish migration guide from legacy endpoints and create troubleshooting KB
Billing: introduce per-endpoint cost banding and update billing catalog entries
Canary config: predefine canary slice policies, traffic weights and rollback thresholds
Legal: update TOS/Customer Data Processing Addendum references if required
Oncall: rotate SRE pager and Solutions Eng for first 72h after canary kickoff
metrics_and_slos: Availability: target 99.9% regional availability for GA tiers
Latency: p95 generation <= 250ms (small prompts), embeddings p95 <= 120ms
Error budget: error_rate <= 0.5% for GA; canary triggers at 1%
Quality: eval-suite pass rate >= 98% on closed-beta datasets; regressions >2% block rollout
Fallback rate: tracked per model; preferred <5% for GA lanes
monitoring_dashboards: edgebundle/overview — traffic, success rate, average latency
edgebundle/fallbacks — percentage of requests routed to fallback and details
edgebundle/error-traces — sampled traces with X-Request-Trace header links
qa_tests: Load test: mixed generate+embed+rerkank traffic profile at 2x expected peak — preflight
Security fuzzing: invalid payloads, huge batches, metadata tampering — run before canary
Safety tests: adversarial prompt injection test-suite and policy enforcer checks
risks_mitigations: Risk: Quality regressions when switching to new model variant. Mitigation: gated eval suites and canary with human-in-the-loop signoff.
Risk: Unexpected cost spikes from large batch embeddings. Mitigation: enforce per-request limits, early rejection, and billing alerts.
Risk: Confusing fallback behavior for customers. Mitigation: include X-Fallback-Info header and clear migration docs describing semantics.
Risk: SSE streaming edge-cases causing client disconnects. Mitigation: default to non-streaming responses when client reports unstable connections; add telemetry to detect disconnect patterns.
post_launch_tasks: Collect 2 weeks of production telemetry and run post-launch evaluation with baseline metrics
Iterate on SDK ergonomics and add a 'migrate-from-legacy' helper in next sprint
Prepare whitepaper with performance/cost tradeoffs for customers considering Dedicated vs Hosted
